system.name: MM-Eval
system.one_liner: A unified evaluation framework for multimodal summaries covering text quality, image-text relevance and image-set diversity, motivated by blind spots of current MSMO metrics.

content.variant_note: a 2 by 2 grid of colour-banded toy-example cards, one per failure of existing metrics, each with a claim header, small score pills, an italic explanation and a takeaway banner
content.argues: Current MSMO metrics are blind to factual errors, to semantically valid image choices, to visual redundancy and to text-image misalignment, because each looks at one modality alone.
content.subject: four toy examples where ROUGE and Image Precision score well or badly for the wrong reason

panels.label: (a) ROUGE: Lexical Overlap ≠ Factual Accuracy
panels.shows: a summary with a wrong date still scores high on ROUGE; takeaway: ROUGE rewards surface similarity

panels.label: (b) Image Precision: Exact Match ≠ Semantic Validity
panels.shows: a semantically valid but non-identical image selection gets IP = 0.50; takeaway: IP penalizes valid non-identical selections

panels.label: (c) Visual Redundancy: No Diversity Penalty
panels.shows: three near-duplicate images get a high IP and no diversity penalty; takeaway: no metric discourages redundancy

panels.label: (d) Cross-Modal Gap: No Alignment Metric
panels.shows: a flooding text and a rally photo score high on ROUGE and IP while alignment is unmeasured

encoding.shape_means: pill = a metric reading or verdict; tinted rounded box = a text sample; rounded thumbnail = an image choice; header bar = claim; bottom band = takeaway
encoding.marker_means: up or down arrow = high or low metric value; tick or cross = valid or not; warning sign = unpenalised or erroneous; question mark = no metric exists
encoding.emphasis: Red words and red pills mark the problem, orange pills mark the gap in current metrics, and the takeaway banner states the lesson in the card hue.

lessons.what_to_learn: State each limitation of existing metrics as a claim header with an inequality, show it on a toy example with coloured pills for what the metric says versus what is true, and close every card with a one-line takeaway banner in the card's hue.
lessons.suits: evaluation or metric papers that motivate a new measure by showing, in a grid of toy examples, where current metrics are blind.

evidence: Figure 1 illustrates these limitations with toy examples.
Outputs are decomposed and assessed via unimodal metrics, each blind to cross-modal coherence.
a limitation we refer to as the “Silo Effect”

summary: MM-Eval is a unified framework for evaluating multimodal summaries by text quality, image-text relevance and image diversity. Figure 1 motivates it with four toy examples of what current MSMO metrics miss. It is a 2 by 2 grid of cards, each with a coloured header that states the claim, a toy example, small score pills and a coloured takeaway banner. (a) ROUGE stays high although a summary changes the date from May 3 to May 5. (b) Image Precision gives 0.50 although the model chose a semantically valid photo. (c) Three near-duplicate photos receive no diversity penalty. (d) High ROUGE and IP hide a flooding text paired with a rally photo.
summary_zh: MM-Eval 用来综合评估多模态摘要的文本质量、图文相关与图像多样性。图一用 2×2 的玩具示例卡片说明现有指标的盲区：ROUGE 看不出日期错误，图像精度惩罚语义有效的选择，没有多样性惩罚，也没有图文对齐指标；每张卡片末尾有要点横幅。
notes: The prior labels listed contribution-mosaic first; because the cards show failures of other people's metrics rather than the paper's own offerings, scope-overview (example-gallery) is primary here and contribution-mosaic (finding-cards) is kept second. A stray 'vs.' label overlaps the italic note in card (b). The photos look AI-generated; their origin is not stated. The figure has no arrows, so relations are all adjacency and colour.
